findings.summary: correction-proof-fixture.json has expectedAnswer=41 (not 42), which is intentional for Criterion 10 proof — the test asserts 42 and will fail until a correction worker restores it
closureGate.ts lines 147-148 contain a duplicated comment line ('could launder its own substantive changes into a closure tail — so the plan and the config are')
authoriseCorrection only emits Edit/Write grants — no Bash, Task or Agent — so the correction worker has no shell and git is structurally unreachable; verified by test assertion
Empty subject commit and empty decision id bindings were previously passing by equality ('' === ''); now explicitly refused in correctionBoundary.ts lines 103-107 with tests proving the refusal

lastInstruction and lastDecisionId are now cleared after use (runner.ts lines 622-624) preventing a subsequent stop from reusing a stale amendment instruction the reviewer never gave for it (CORR-STALE-DECISION-ID)

correctionBoundary refuses paths containing '..', absolute paths starting with '/', and Windows drive letters; segment-based prefix matching prevents 'agent-secrets' matching 'agent' boundary — all tested

Only the provider handle is taken from a session record on rejoin; briefPath and briefId are recomputed, preventing a worker that wrote its own session record from redirecting the next rejoin — tested in loopRunner.test.ts

Phase scope is now projected into the structured plan record during materialisation (planApproval.ts) and added to the plan schema, making the approved scope machine-readable rather than lost at activation
